title: Grain Merchandising Rule: The Credit Factor on Loads Run Straight Through to the Buyer
content:
A load run straight through to the buyer never crosses the cooperative's own scale into store, and bushels credited to a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts on that footing are credited at a factor rather than at their full ticket weight. The factor turns on how many such loads stand and where they were received.

**1.** Where two or more loads were run straight through to the buyer and every one of them was received at the facility the contract calls for, the factor is 1.0, and the loads credit their net bushels in full.

**2.** Where two or more loads were run straight through but they were not all received at that facility, the factor is 0.99.

**3.** Where neither of those holds — that is, where fewer than two such loads stand — the factor is 0.975.

## The bands read against one another

| Straight-through loads standing | All received at the facility the contract calls for | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Yes | 1.0 |
| 3 | No | 0.99 |
| 2 | Yes | 1.0 |
| 2 | No | 0.99 |
| 1 | Either way | 0.975 |
| 0 | Either way | 0.975 |

A single straight-through load takes 0.975 whatever facility received it, because the first band and the second both ask for two loads before anything else is read.

## Illustration on hypothetical loads

Two loads run straight through carry 3,000 net bushels between them and were both received at the facility the contract calls for. They credit 3,000 bushels. Had one of them been received elsewhere, they would credit 2,970 bushels. Had there been only one such load, of 1,500 net bushels, it would credit 1,462.50 bushels.
